findings.body:
**Pass `--no-follow-tags` to the leased push.**

`gitPushAtomic` does not disable `push.followTags`. When the operator's global or repository config sets `push.followTags=true`, `git push` also publishes annotated tags that are reachable from the pushed commits and missing on the remote. Those tags have no `LeasedUpdate` and bypass the supplied update set. Add `--no-follow-tags` to the push argv so only the supplied refspecs are published.

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
     [
       'push',
+      '--no-follow-tags',
       '--atomic',
       '--porcelain',
       '--no-verify',
       ...leases,
       '--end-of-options',
       url,
       ...updates.map((u) => u.refspec),
     ],
```

</details>
findings.title: Pass `--no-follow-tags` to the leased push.

findings.body:
**Block the `ext` transport in the remote push and lookup environment.**

`assertPushUrl` checks only the input string. Git applies `url.<base>.insteadOf` after that check, and the rewritten URL can select the `ext::` transport. `GIT_HARDEN` sets no protocol restriction, and `gitRemoteEnv` does not set `protocol.ext.allow`. If local or global Git config sets `protocol.ext.allow=always` and an `insteadOf` rewrite, `gitPushAtomic` and `gitLsRemoteRef` can execute the rewritten command. The trigger is repository or global Git config, not tree content. The file header treats that config as untrusted. Adding `protocol.ext.allow=never` to the same environment list blocks the rewritten transport. HTTPS and local-path remotes keep working.

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
   const config: [string, string][] = [
     ['credential.helper', ''],
     ['core.askPass', ''],
+    ['protocol.ext.allow', 'never'],
   ];
```

</details>
findings.title: Block the `ext` transport in the remote push and lookup environment.

findings.body:
**Scrub the shallow and graft file variables from the Git child environment.**

`gitEnv()` removes only the variables in `SCRUBBED_ENV`. `GIT_SHALLOW_FILE` and `GIT_GRAFT_FILE` are not in that list, so an inherited value reaches every Git call. Git reads both variables and applies them to commit parents and ancestry. A shallow file that lists `C` treats `C` as a root, so `gitRangeCommits(A, C)` can omit `B` and report `C` without its real parent. `gitIsAncestor` can return a wrong answer for the same reason. `GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS` only disables replace refs and does not cover these two variables. Add both names to `SCRUBBED_ENV`, as the file already does for the other repository-redirecting variables.

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
   'GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES',
+  'GIT_GRAFT_FILE',
+  'GIT_SHALLOW_FILE',
   'GIT_NAMESPACE',
```

</details>
findings.title: Scrub the shallow and graft file variables from the Git child environment.
